content:
maria: heads-up — us-west GPU pool hit sustained 92-97% utilization last 30m, streaming requests are seeing stalls while non-stream batches are queued. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/in/gpu/us-west

aj: saw this too. p99 of streaming responses spiked from 120ms -> 1.8s. non-stream queue depth jumped. looks like admission isn't favoring streaming when pool saturates.

simon: fwiw we have per-route rate limits but they don't account for stream vs non-stream shape. current allocator treats them the same and uses a single concurrency cap.

maria: proposal: soft-reserve X% of concurrency for streaming workloads in each GPU pool, but allow borrow when idle. reduces streaming tail at little cost to throughput.

elaine: need to be careful: enterprise customers with reserved capacity will expect their non-stream SLAs preserved. any soft reserve must be policy-aware (route tags, customer tier).

aj: agree. rough config prototype I tested locally:

```yaml
admission:
  pools:
    - name: us-west-gpu
      total_slots: 400
      streaming_reserved_pct: 15   # soft reserve for streaming
      allow_stream_borrow: true
      borrow_threshold_ms: 200    # allow borrow if streaming p50 < 200ms
```

aj: with that, in the sim we pushed p99_stream down ~400ms without throughput loss.

simon: how do we detect borrow safely? race conditions might let non-stream steal when streaming suddenly surges. need a short retraction window and a preemption signal.

maria: idea: when borrow happens attach a non-blocking preempt token to borrowed slots; if streaming queue grows above N, preempt oldest non-stream workers at soft-grace checkpoint (end of current sequence). avoid killing long-running gen mid-token.

elaine: also think about billing impact — if reserved streaming reduces non-stream throughput, tail customers might see slower batch jobs and open tickets. include a metric in console: per-customer lost throughput from soft-reserve.

simon: could gate this behind a feature flag per-pool + per-tenant. default off for enterprise pools.

maria: ops checklist if we roll this:
- enable soft-reserve in us-west canary pool (non-prod first)
- watch metrics: streaming_p99_latency, nonstream_queue_depth, borrowing_rate, preempt_count
- set auto-rollback if streaming_p99 increases or nonstream_queue_growth > 30% sustained

aj: quick CLI I ran to simulate borrow: `rbctl admit --pool us-west-gpu --kind streaming --weight 1.15` — matches earlier sim. produced logs:
```
[2026-03-18T12:03:21Z] admit: pool=us-west-gpu kind=streaming action=borrow slots=8 from=nonstream reason=soft-reserve
[2026-03-18T12:03:22Z] preempt-signal: pool=us-west-gpu tgt=job-9182 grace=token-boundary
```
deploy-bot: deploy request accepted: rollout/soft-reserve-canary -> eng-infra-us-west (user=maria)

maria: launching canary now for 30m. will reduce streaming_reserved_pct to 10% if we see nonstream queue pain.

simon: one more thought — network egress congestion also correlated with stalls earlier this week. if borrow masks network bottleneck we'll be chasing the wrong thing. ensure we correlate with net tx/rx metrics.

aj: yup, correlating now. early view: tx throughput from pods stays flat while GPU busy increases -> likely compute-bound not network.

elaine: ok. keep me posted. if preempt_count > 5 within 10m for any single tenant, auto-disable for that tenant. ops-sla requirement.

maria: noted. i'll post short postmortem if any anomalies during canary. starting now. :rocket:
